svg.title: Eventhouse/KQL Hot Cache vs Cold Storage Internals
svg.desc: An internals diagram tracing one ingested record through Eventhouse storage. Records land first in the premium-tier hot cache governed by the caching policy, and remain queryable there for fast, low-latency access. In parallel, the full retention window is held in a separate, independently billed standard-tier store governed by the retention policy. If OneLake availability is enabled, an adaptive-batching decision delays the OneLake write until enough data accumulates for optimally sized Parquet files, trading latency for file-size efficiency. A warning node covers the DDL operations blocked while OneLake availability is active. A second warning node describes the three-stage capacity throttling ladder — proactive, reactive, and extreme-reactive — that fires when query and ingestion demand exceeds available capacity.
svg.text: Eventhouse / KQL — Hot Path vs Cold Path Internals
Ingestion decision routing · caching & retention policies · update-policy transforms · throttling ladder

g.title: Record ingested into KQL database — An event record arrives and is organized by arrival time for fast, indexed querying.
Hot cache tier (caching policy) — Premium-tier storage holding the hot dataset for fast queries, governed by the caching policy.

g.text: Governs how long data stays in premium-tier cache
Shorter window = lower premium spend, same total history
Trigger table → transform function → target table,
executed automatically as new rows land in the cache
Feeds materialized views for pre-aggregated hot reads
Runs inside the hot path — before data ages to retention
Evaluates live time-series in place — no copy or export
Direct pivot from dashboard alert to live KQL investigation
Compute node ready in 5–10 s after idle — autoscaled
Design latency-sensitive pipelines around this warm-up
Query demand > capacity? → see throttling ladder below

g.title: Cold standard tier (retention policy) — Standard-tier storage holding the full retention window, governed by the retention policy.

g.text: Governs the full queryable history window
ADLS-hot-equivalent billing; higher latency than cache reads

g.title: Adaptive batching to OneLake — OneLake writes are delayed until enough data accumulates for optimally sized Parquet files.

g.text: Delta Lake Consumers (no data copy, no extra charge)
Power BI Direct Lake · Warehouse · Lakehouse · Spark notebooks
Retention policy soft-deletes the OneLake copy in lockstep

g.title: Trap: blocked DDL while OneLake-available — Rename, type change, row-level security, and delete/purge are blocked while OneLake availability is active.
OneLake availability enabled? — Whether the table's data is also exposed as Delta in OneLake, at the database or table level.
g.text: Rename table · change column type · row-level security ·
delete/purge rows — all blocked. Re-enable ⇒ full backfill
Shortcut into KQL DB → external_table() function, not native
Capacity Pressure Decision Ladder — applies across both paths

g.title: Three-stage capacity throttling ladder — Proactive, reactive, and extreme-reactive throttling stages fire as capacity pressure escalates.
